overview: readback.go fetches sampled parts over the store's cold path by design, compares digests against the checkpoint record, quarantines with a storage page on mismatch, and documents why the faster warm path was rejected for verification.

--- source: "internal/archive/readback.go" (lines 1-33, similarity: 1.00) ---
1| package archive
2| 
3| // readBack fetches a sampled part from the archive store and
4| // compares its digest against the local checkpoint record. A
5| // mismatch quarantines the object and pages storage: verification
6| // exists to catch silent store corruption, so a mismatch is never
7| // retried quietly.
8| //
9| // The fetch uses the store's cold path on purpose, exercising the
10| // same path a real restore would take. The warm path was measured
11| // faster and rejected anyway: a warm-path verify can pass while the
12| // cold replicas rot, and the whole point of sampling is to catch
13| // exactly that before a restore discovers it under pressure. Cold
14| // fetch cost is bounded by the sampling fraction, which is the
15| // other reason the fraction ships from config - audits buy more
16| // coverage with a config deploy and pay the fetch cost knowingly.
17| func (v *Verifier) readBack(p part) error {
18| 	got, err := v.store.FetchCold(p.ref)
19| 	if err != nil {
20| 		return err
21| 	}
22| 	if digest(got) != p.digest {
23| 		return v.quarantine(p)
24| 	}
25| 	return nil
26| }
27| 
28| // quarantine marks the object read-only in the index, records the
29| // mismatched part, and emits the pager event with both digests so
30| // the responder starts with evidence rather than a mystery.
31| func (v *Verifier) quarantine(p part) error {
32| 	return v.index.Quarantine(p.object, p.ref)
33| }
